Definition: from G4151; non-carnal, i.e. (humanly) ethereal (as opposed to gross), or (dæmoniacally) a spirit (concretely), or (divinely) supernatural, regenerate, religious:--spiritual. Compare G5591.
BiblicalUsage: Pneumatikos means spiritual, of the Spirit, not of the flesh. Paul speaks in words taught by the Spirit, comparing spiritual things with spiritual, in 1 Corinthians 2:13, yet calls the Corinthians carnal, not spiritual, in 1 Corinthians 3:1. There is a natural body and a spiritual body, says 1 Corinthians 15:44, and our wrestling is against spiritual wickedness in Ephesians 6:12. The spiritual are to restore the fallen in meekness, says Galatians 6:1.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe spiritual is not a feeling but a nature — the Spirit's work in me against the flesh. That is why I hold that the test of spirituality is not gifts but gentleness toward a fallen brother.
